## Chatbot analysis v1

```{r}
#libraries
library(dplyr)
library(BradleyTerry2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

Read in the data

```{r}
d <- read.csv("data.csv")
head(d)
```

Calculate percentage win rates

```{r}
# count wins per model
model_wins <- d %>%
  filter(winner %in% c("model_a", "model_b")) %>%
  mutate(winner_model = ifelse(winner == "model_a", model_a, model_b)) %>%
  count(winner_model, name = "wins")

# Count appearances
model_appearances <- d %>%
  select(model_a, model_b) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), values_to = "model") %>%
  count(model, name = "appearances")

# Merge wins and appearances
performance_summary <- model_appearances %>%
  left_join(model_wins, by = c("model" = "winner_model")) %>%
  mutate(wins = replace_na(wins, 0),
         win_rate = wins / appearances) %>%
  arrange(desc(win_rate))

print(performance_summary)
```

Plot win rate of models

```{r}
top10 <- performance_summary %>%
  arrange(desc(win_rate)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 30)

ggplot(top10, aes(x = reorder(model, win_rate), y = win_rate)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Top 10 Chatbot Models by Win Rate",
    x = "Model",
    y = "Win Rate (Proportion of Judged Wins)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10, margin = margin(r = 8))
  )


```

Use logistic regression to quantify the performance differences between models while adjusting for factors like opponent or judge. A binary logistic regression was used, with model1 and model 2 as predictors.

```{r}
# Filter to usable rows
df_use <- d %>%
  filter(winner %in% c("model_a", "model_b"))

# Binary outcome: 1 = model_a won, 0 = model_b won
df_use <- df_use %>%
  mutate(outcome = ifelse(winner == "model_a", 1, 0))

# Create indicator variables for model identities
df_use <- df_use %>%
  mutate(
    model_a_factor = factor(model_a),
    model_b_factor = factor(model_b)
  )

# Use model1 and model2 as predictors
model <- glm(outcome ~ model_a_factor + model_b_factor, data = df_use, family = binomial)
summary(model)
```

Bradley-Terry Model (specifically for pairwise comparison data)

```{r}
# Step 1: Prepare pairwise outcome data
df_bt <- d %>%
  filter(winner %in% c("model_a", "model_b")) %>%
  mutate(
    winner_model = ifelse(winner == "model_a", model_a, model_b),
    loser_model  = ifelse(winner == "model_a", model_b, model_a)
  )

# Step 2: Ensure both winner and loser columns are factors with the same levels
all_models <- union(df_bt$winner_model, df_bt$loser_model)
df_bt <- df_bt %>%
  mutate(
    winner_model = factor(winner_model, levels = all_models),
    loser_model  = factor(loser_model,  levels = all_models)
  )

# Step 3: Create player list for BTm format
players <- data.frame(model = factor(all_models))  # model ID factor

# Step 4: Fit the Bradley-Terry model
bt_model <- BTm(
  outcome = rep(1, nrow(df_bt)),
  player1 = df_bt$winner_model,
  player2 = df_bt$loser_model,
  id = "model",
  data = players
)

summary(bt_model)
```
